lectures.title: Physical divisions of Andhra Pradesh: boundaries, hills, coast and plateau

parts.t: Boundaries of Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema
items: **State area:** 1,62,970 sq km; Andhra Pradesh is the 7th largest state.

parts.t: The Eastern Ghats: the major hill system
items: **Eastern Ghats:** the major hill / mountain system of AP, lying between the western side of the Coastal Plain and the eastern side of the Deccan Plateau.
**Maximum height of the Eastern Ghats:** at Chintapalli (Paderu).
**Lowest-height hills:** the lowest hills of the Eastern Ghats merge with Dolphin Nose, Visakhapatnam (Dolphin Nose area); Dolphin Nose height is 335 m.
**Papikonda Ranges:** spread over the Godavari districts; average height 915 m.
**Khondalite hills / mountains:** the bauxite-bearing highest mountains of the Eastern Ghats are of Khondalite rocks, mainly in erstwhile Visakhapatnam and East Godavari.
Highest peak in the Eastern Ghats
**Highest peak of Andhra Pradesh:** Arma Konda (Aroma), 1680 m at Chintapalli; Jindhagada (1690 m, Araku) is the other name and height given for this highest peak of the Eastern Ghats.

items: Listed as the northern geographical extent of AP

Andhra Pradesh; Eastern Ghats; South / Southern AP
Northern end of the long mountain-pass zone (Seshachalam → Nallamala)
**Nallamala Hills:** between the Krishna and Pennar Rivers; broadly N–S; parallel to the Coromandel Coast. Srisailam is situated on the flat top of the Nallamala Hills.
**Seshachalam Hills:** Eastern Ghats; associated with Tirupati and the Lord Venkateswara Temple: the Tirupati temple lies in the Seshachalam range.
Veda & Avathi arise in its eastern part and join to form Vedavathi

parts.t: Mountain passes of the Eastern Ghats
items: **Long Mountain Pass of the Eastern Ghats:** between the Seshachalam Hills and extending northwards to the Nallamala Hills; the mountain pass is more than 300 km long.
**Important towns on the pass:** Venkatagiri → Badvel → Porumamilla → Giddalur → Markapur.
**Ganjikunta:** a notable mountain pass located in the Eastern Ghats.
**Location:** Eastern Ghats, connecting sections between the Seshachalam and Nallamala hill ranges.
**Function:** acts as a geographical break dividing parts of the uplands and lowlands in the region.
**Terrain:** characterized by dry deciduous forests and rocky elevations typical of peninsular India's eastern hill ranges.

parts.t: The coast and the Bay of Bengal
items: **Coastal Andhra:** located along the Bay of Bengal, the eastern boundary of Andhra Pradesh.
**Coastal Plains:** from the Eastern Ghats to the Bay of Bengal, extending from erstwhile Srikakulam to Nellore.
AP has the **3rd longest coastline** in India: **1053.07 km**.
**Yarada Hills:** on the sea coast of Visakhapatnam (merging point: Dolphin Nose); they give natural protection to Visakhapatnam Port.
**Eastern Ghats:** sea-nack-like projections into the sea, extending about 950 km from Mahendragiri in the north to Pulicat Lake in the south.
**Pulicat Lake:** a salt-water lake at the southern end of the coast; the Penna meets the sea further north, near Utukuru.
Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, YSR, Annamayya, Tirupati & Chittoor
**Type of disaster:** an earthquake is a geological disaster; it is not an atmospheric natural disaster.
Earthquake origin point inside the Earth
Point directly above the focus on the surface
Earthquake measuring device (used to measure intensity)
Preferred over Richter for large quakes
Used in India & many European countries
**India's seismic zones:** 4 zones. **AP seismic zones:** Zone 2 and Zone 3.
Entire North-East, J&K, Ladakh, Himachal, Uttarakhand, parts of Bihar, Kutch (Gujarat), Andaman & Nicobar
Delhi, parts of J&K / HP, North Bihar, parts of UP, Punjab, Rajasthan, Maharashtra
Remaining Indo-Gangetic plains, coastal areas, Kerala, Goa, parts of MP, Rajasthan
One of the earliest well-studied great quakes
One of the largest ever recorded
Major turning point → led to DM Act 2005
**Nodal ministry for earthquakes:** Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). **Technical agency:** National Centre for Seismology (under MoES).
Policy guidelines, National Earthquake Risk Mitigation Project
IS 1893 – Earthquake resistant design of structures
Detailed risk mapping of cities (Delhi, Guwahati, etc.)
Specialised search & rescue (Collapsed Structure Search & Rescue – CSSR)
**Earthquake mitigation:** reframing building-construction guidelines and their implementation.
**Non-structural examples:** seismic microzonation, building codes, awareness.
**Landslide:** mass movement of rocks, debris or earth down mountain slopes or riverbanks.
**Definition:** rapid downward movement of rock, soil, debris or vegetation under the influence of gravity.
**Nature:** a geological / hydro-meteorological hazard; may occur gradually or suddenly without warning.
**Triggers:** the main trigger in India is heavy rainfall; the major rainfall trigger mentioned is prolonged rainfall.
**Cloudburst connection:** prolonged rainfall → heavy landslides; a landslide can block rivers → downstream havoc.
About **12.6%** of India's land area (≈ **0.42 million sq km**) is landslide-prone.
**Most vulnerable regions in India:** Himalayas & Western Ghats (Himalayas + Western Ghats + Northeast).
Sikkim, Arunachal, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya
Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Goa, Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris)
**Geological Survey of India (GSI):** HQ Kolkata; the nodal agency, technical agency and forecasting organisation for landslides.
**GSI's role:** landslide forecasting, landslide studies & hazard mapping, seismic & geological hazard assessment.
**Nodal ministry for landslides:** Ministry of Mines.
**NDMA Guidelines:** Guidelines on Management of Landslides and Snow Avalanches (2009).
**Key strategy document:** National Landslide Risk Management Strategy (2019).
**Key initiatives:** National Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (NLSM) by GSI, the important mapping programme; National Landslide Forecasting Centre.
Retaining walls, slope stabilisation, rock bolting, wire mesh, drainage improvement, slope grading
Landslide Hazard Zonation (LHZ) mapping, Early Warning Systems (early warning), land-use regulation, afforestation, awareness
Restrict construction in high-risk zones; enforce mountain-specific building codes
